title: You didn’t ask a casual question. You asked something that has divided churches, families, and entire cultures—and most people answer it by either softening the truth or weaponizing it.
paragraphs: You didn’t ask a casual question. You asked something that has divided churches, families, and entire cultures—and most people answer it by either softening the truth or weaponizing it.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

God is not confused about this.
And He is not silent either.
The real tension is not whether God speaks on LGBTQ+ issues.
It’s whether people are willing to hear what He actually says—without editing Him.
It usually starts quietly.

Not with a parade.
Not with a declaration.
Just a thought.

A feeling you didn’t choose.
An attraction you didn’t plan.
And then the question comes in:
“Did God really say this is wrong?”

Because if He didn’t…
then you don’t have to wrestle.
You don’t have to surrender.
You don’t have to change.
But if He did…
Everything changes.
Scripture does not begin with identity politics.
It begins with design.
“In the beginning, God created them male and female.” (Genesis 1:27)

That wasn’t random.
That wasn’t cultural.
That was intentional.
Marriage, from the very start, was defined:
“A man shall leave his father and mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.” (Genesis 2:24)
Before sin ever entered the world, God already established the pattern.

Not as restriction.
But as order.
Then sin entered.
And everything distorted.
Desires included.
Not just sexual ones—all of them.

You feel anger you shouldn’t.
You crave things that destroy you.
You think thoughts you know aren’t right.
Sexual desire is not exempt from that fall.
And this is where honesty matters.
Because Scripture doesn’t isolate one group—it exposes all of humanity.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)

That includes heterosexual sin.
That includes pride.
That includes lust.
That includes you.
And yes—it includes same-sex sexual behavior.
Now here’s where many people either harden or walk away.
Because the Bible speaks directly.
“You shall not lie with a male as with a woman; it is an abomination.” (Leviticus 18:22)
People rush to dismiss that as “Old Testament.”
But then the New Testament speaks again—clearly.
“For this reason God gave them up to dishonorable passions… men committing shameless acts with men…” (Romans 1:26–27)
And again:
“Do not be deceived… neither the sexually immoral… nor men who practice homosexuality… will inherit the kingdom of God.” (1 Corinthians 6:9–10)
Read that again.

Not to attack.
Not to shame.
But to understand the weight.
God is not ambiguous about behavior.
But here’s the part many people never hear—because it doesn’t fit either extreme.
The verse doesn’t end there.
“And such were some of you. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ…” (1 Corinthians 6:11)
Such were some of you.
That means transformation is real.

Not behavior management.
Not suppression.
Transformation.
This is where everything shifts.
Because the Bible does not say:
“Fix yourself and come to God.”
It says:
“Come to Christ, and He will make you new.”
Jesus didn’t come to affirm sin.
He came to save sinners.
“Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more.” (John 8:11)
Notice both:

No condemnation.
No permission to continue.
Grace and truth.
Together.
So what does God say about LGBTQ+?
He says:
Your desires do not define you.
Your feelings are not your authority.
Your identity is not rooted in sexuality.
Your identity is found in Christ—or it is lost entirely.
And here’s the uncomfortable truth most people avoid:
You don’t go to hell for being tempted.
You don’t go to hell for struggling.
You go to hell for rejecting the truth and refusing the Savior.
The same is true for every sin.
Not just this one.
God saw it.

The confusion.
The secret thoughts.
The moments you justified it.
You knew.

You felt the tension.
You felt something wasn’t aligned.
And maybe you buried it.
Maybe you found voices that told you what you wanted to hear.
But deep down…
You knew.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
And now you’re here, reading this—not by accident.
Because this isn’t about winning an argument.
It’s about your soul.
There are two paths in front of you.
One says:
“God accepts me as I am. I don’t need to change.”

It feels easier.
It feels affirming.
But it leads you further from truth.
The other says:
“I don’t understand everything… but if God says it, I will trust Him.”
That path costs you something.
Sometimes everything.
But it leads to life.
Jesus said:
“If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.” (Matthew 16:24)
Deny himself.
Not just actions.
Desires.
Identity claims.
Everything.
This is not just about LGBTQ+.
This is about surrender.
Because every follower of Christ has something they must lay down.
For some, it’s pride.
For others, it’s lust.
For others, it’s control.
For you…
you already know what it is.
And here’s the hope that changes everything:
When you lay it down…
you are not left empty.
You are filled with something greater.
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.” (2 Corinthians 5:17)
Not improved.
New.
This is where most people stop reading.
Because now it’s not theoretical anymore.
Now it’s personal.
If this stirred something in you—don’t ignore it.
Say it plainly:
“I want truth, even if it costs me.”
Or be honest:
“I’m not ready to let this go.”
But don’t pretend neutrality.
There isn’t any.

There are deeper teachings, harder truths, and real discipleship waiting—this is just the beginning. If you’re serious about walking this out, about understanding Scripture without compromise and without confusion, step into it fully:
Not for information.
For transformation.
And if this hit you… say it.
Not perfectly.
Just honestly.
